To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we can train an inverse graphics model to disentangle a GAN latent space by utilizing an off-the-shelve differentiable renderer, (2) our model outperforms state of the art in terms of quantitative metrics and human evaluation, (3) the disentangled space can be used to generate novel 3D content, and (4) the disentanglement can be used for novel view synthesis

(1) we propose a novel approach that combines GANs and differentiable rendering to train an inverse model that is capable of predicting 3D properties of objects from a single photograph and (2) we show how this inverse model can be used to disentangle a generative model's latent space, allowing for the first time to interpret and manipulate 3D properties using the latent code of GANs

1) GANs can be utilized to train an inverse 3D graphics network, 2) this network can be used to disentangle GANs into interpretable 2D/3D representations, 3) these representations can be used for 3D reasoning and controllable rendering.

the question of whether GANs implicitly learn 3D knowledge and, if so, whether this knowledge can be extracted to improve inverse graphics and 3D rendering.
how to make GANs interpretable by leveraging differentiable renderers, and how to make differentiable renderers learnable from GANs.
the following question: Can we leverage the power of GANs to learn interpretable 3d representations? We believe our work provides a step towards the answer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose a new approach for training an inverse graphics network by leveraging GANs and a differentiable renderer.

we present the first method that can disentangle the latent code of a GAN into interpretable 2D and 3D properties, and that we demonstrate the utility of our approach for both inverse graphics and interpretable 3d neural rendering.
the proposed method enables a new paradigm of 3D reasoning and 3D neural rendering, where a 3D model is not explicitly represented but rather inferred from the image space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that GANs are able to acquire 3d knowledge, and we propose a method to extract this 3d knowledge and disentangle it in a physically interpretable manner.
we propose to leverage the power of Generative Adverserial Networks (GAN) and the recent differentiable rendering technique to achieve the goal of interpretable 3d neural rendering.
we are able to extract 3D knowledge from generative models by combining differentiable renderers and GANs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
generative models, trained on a large amount of unstructured data, can learn 3D knowledge that is not only useful for 3D reconstruction, but can also be disentangled and used as a 3D renderer.
GANs implicitly learn 3D knowledge that can be extracted and disentangled to enable interpretable 3d neural rendering.
